_comment: Hand-authored RAM map. One entry per named byte or range; every entry says how it is known. status: 'confirmed' = read from the code that uses it (evidence names the routine); 'checked' = also checked against a savestate or a run; 'lead' = a reading of the code or of one use, not established. The generated cross-reference (tools/tgl/ram.py) is shown beside each entry and is not claimed here.

ranges.name: Zero page
ranges.what: Scratch, pointers, game state, the pads, the scroll engine's counters.

ranges.name: PPU queue, stack and small buffers
ranges.what: The PPU write queue grows up from $0100; the CPU stack grows down from $01FF. The score, the palette shadow and the status screen's buffers sit in the middle.

ranges.name: OAM shadow
ranges.what: Sprite memory, DMA'd to the PPU every frame (bank 7 NMI).

ranges.name: Sound state
ranges.what: The sound engine of bank 0: flags, a busy mask, the APU register shadow and seven soft channels.

ranges.name: Stage and progress state
ranges.what: Corridor overlay slots, the loaded metatile sets, per-area flags, weapon levels, keys, the row of metatiles being built, and the labyrinth move history.

ranges.name: Object slots
ranges.what: 24 slots x 32 fields: field f of slot s is at $0500 + $18 f + s. See the field table.

entries.name: jump_table_ptr
entries.what: The inline jump-table routines pop their return address into it and fetch entry k at +2k ($9F10 and the copies in banks 6 and 7). The random routine also reads $0000,Y as noise. The pad reader $D626 uses them too: bit 1 of each $4016 / $4017 read is rotated into $00 / $01 (expansion-port bits), beside the ordinary bit 0 into $F5 / $F6.

entries.name: pad_prev_bit1
entries.what: The previous read's $00 / $01, kept by the pad routine ($D64C-$D674): the pads are read again until two reads in a row agree on all four bytes ($F5, $F6, $00 / $01 against $02 / $03). The usual reason for such a loop is a DMC sample fetch stealing a cycle mid-read; this game runs the DMC as its split timer, so the guard fits, but that reason is an inference.

entries.name: live_bank
entries.what: The PRG bank currently selected. Every bank-switch routine writes it.

entries.name: dmc_rate
entries.what: The DMC timer's rate index, reloaded into $4010 by the IRQ and tuned between $81 and $89 to land the raster split.

entries.name: decomp_bank
entries.what: The bank holding the tile block being decompressed: stored when a block is armed ($D81C, from the caller's bank argument) and switched to at the start of every decompressor pass ($DB55); bank 6 $8022 initialises it to 5.

entries.name: decomp_run_value
entries.what: The tile decompressor: the value of the run section being expanded ($DBFB), written $08 times into the output buffer.

entries.name: decomp_run_count
entries.what: The tile decompressor: how many more bytes of the current run to write ($DC06 loads the count, $DC0E counts it down).

entries.name: decomp_header
entries.what: The tile decompressor's escape byte ($09) and mirror byte ($0A) for the block it is decoding.

entries.name: decomp_flags
entries.what: Decompressor state: bit 7 flips at each escape byte; a non-zero value, with $A5 and $20, makes the wait routine $D7C3 keep waiting.

entries.name: decomp_src
entries.what: The decompressor's source pointer in the ROM bank.

entries.name: decomp_dst
entries.what: The destination PPU address the decompressor writes tile bytes to (copied from $18/$19 when a block is armed).

entries.name: scratch
entries.what: Scratch. The far-call trampoline saves A and Y here.

entries.name: farcall_ptr
entries.what: The far-call trampoline's pointer to its three inline bytes (bank, target low, target high).

entries.name: args
entries.what: Arguments and scratch. For the $D5CC queue-a-fill helper, $15 is the count byte (bit 7: step 32) and $14 the fill value. For a spawn, $15 is the type.

entries.name: src_ptr
entries.what: A source pointer: the screen-script renderer's script, the inline-string helpers' return address, a structure's tiles.

entries.name: ppu_addr
entries.what: A PPU address (low, high) for the queue producers; also reused as an object's x/y or an index in some handlers.

entries.name: ptr2
entries.what: A second pointer or PPU address pair: the status screen's map walk builds the map address into it, and the rectangle blit's loop positions use it.

entries.name: sound_ptr
entries.what: The sound engine's pointer into the current channel's stream (and a note sequence).

entries.name: sound_tmp
entries.what: The sound engine's scratch: the pitch slide's delta (16 bits), a volume, or a pointer to a note sequence or an envelope.

entries.name: queue_len
entries.what: The PPU queue's fill state: $21 is the byte offset of the next entry, $20 counts flushes.

entries.name: queue_end
entries.what: Offset of the next free byte in the PPU queue. The space check $D6C0 refuses an entry that would reach $51, and, while $A5 is not 0, one that would reach $31.

entries.name: ppu_read_prev
entries.what: The attribute read-modify-write ($DE20-$DE61) reads the PPU byte twice and repeats until two reads agree: $22 is the previous value read.

entries.name: ppu_rmw_saved_x
entries.what: X (the queue cursor) saved across the attribute read-modify-write loop.

entries.name: queue_saved_flushes
entries.what: The PPU queue's reservation ($D6E0): $20 is saved here and cleared, and if $21 (the next-free offset) is unchanged afterwards $24 is kept, otherwise zeroed ($D6F4); $D6FE restores $20 = $24 + 1 when the entry is committed. So an NMI that drains the queue between reserve and commit is noticed. Purpose read from the code, not run.

entries.name: queue_reserved
entries.what: Length of the queue entry being reserved ($D6E0), added to $21 when it is committed ($D6F7).

entries.name: ppustatus_snapshot
entries.what: PPUSTATUS read once per NMI.

entries.name: art_stream
entries.what: The art-load stream: $27 is its position (bit 7 set while one runs), $28/$29 its pointer - the default $A497, a miniboss's, or the one command 7 names.

entries.name: rng_state
entries.what: The random number state: $F9D1 mixes it with the stack pointer, $41 and bytes of ROM and RAM; the IRQ stirs it ($DCE8).

entries.name: frame_counter
entries.what: Counts NMIs. The wait-frames routine $FFD1 clears it and the wait loops $DA9A/$DAD8 spin on it.
entries.evidence: bank 7 $DA9A-$DAE0, $FFD1; the NES model's frame loop depends on it

entries.name: retry_unused
entries.what: Cleared at game start and read in the death test (bank 6 $8239) with $48 and $49; no write other than the clear was found, so it is always 0.

entries.name: boot_flag
entries.what: Branched on in the boot path; set to 0 by a new game and by the TGL back door.

entries.name: game_mode
entries.what: Mode bits - see the table below.
entries.evidence: many; the bits are listed with their writers

entries.name: dpad_cell
entries.what: The D-pad as a 3 x 3 cell index 0-8 (3 x horizontal + vertical, 4 = nothing held), from the table at bank 7 $DB22 every frame. The Wave Attack in a corridor picks its heading from it ($8837[$32]).

entries.name: fire_counter
entries.what: The main gun's countdown: reset to 1 when B is released, otherwise counts down each frame and a shot leaves when it reaches 0, then it reloads from $39.
entries.evidence: bank 3 $8E04-$8E1B; run with B held on the NES model

entries.name: obj_slot
entries.what: The object slot the bank 6 loop is on (0-23).
entries.evidence: bank 6 $81F5-$8204, $8227; slot order run on the NES model

entries.name: obj_loop_count
entries.what: Counts object-loop passes; its bit 1 selects the slot order for the pass (0-4 then 5 up to 23, or 0-4 then 23 down to 5), so the order flips every two frames.
entries.evidence: bank 6 $81FB-$8212, table $81DD; order run on the NES model

entries.name: obj_current
entries.what: The slot whose handler is running (the loop's X, kept for the handler).

entries.name: temp_38
entries.what: Two uses: the metasprite drawer's saved X, and the aim routine's direction flags ($F863).

entries.name: shot_delay
entries.what: Frames between the player's shots, from $87CE[$6B].

entries.name: chip_tier
entries.what: The chip tier 0-3 that shapes the main gun's shot: 0 under 100 chips, 1 at 100-199, 2 at 200-2047, 3 from 2048. Recomputed by bank 7 $E213 whenever the chip total changes (spend or pick-up), read by every shot every frame.

entries.name: gun_slots
entries.what: How many of object slots 1-4 the main gun may use, from $FDCA[$3C] (4 with no weapon selected, then 3 2 3 3 3 3 2 3 3 3 2 3). The selected weapon's own objects take the slots above that.

entries.name: weapon
entries.what: The selected weapon: 0 none, 1-12.

entries.name: weapon_level
entries.what: The selected weapon's level, 0-3.

entries.name: uses_left
entries.what: Chips / $45, or $04AF for weapon 12.

entries.name: weapon_fee_timer
entries.what: Counts down once per frame per weapon object; at 0 the weapon is charged its chip cost and the timer reloads with 60 (120 when two objects share it).
entries.evidence: bank 6 $8616-$8641; chip timeline run on the NES model

entries.name: score_dirty
entries.what: Set when the score changes; the HUD routine redraws the score once and clears it.

entries.name: frame_tick
entries.what: Incremented once per game frame by the main loops; handlers mask it for periodic actions (a shot every 16 or 32 frames).

entries.name: box_step
entries.what: Which step of the item-box schedule is next, 0-7: an index into the thresholds at bank 1 $8219 and the contents at $8221.
entries.evidence: bank 1 $817D-$8190, $81E4-$8209; run on the real routine

entries.name: box_counter
entries.what: The weighted kill counter. It counts up by each kill's weight; when it reaches the step's threshold an item box is released. Zeroed at game start only.
entries.evidence: bank 1 $817F-$818D, $8190; bank 0 $8072; run on the real routine

entries.name: box_rotation
entries.what: Counts the boxes of step 7 so its contents rotate through bank 1 $8229 (4 entries).

entries.name: chips_per_use
entries.what: Chips spent per shot of the selected weapon.

entries.name: chip_level
entries.what: The chip capacity level, 0-10 (Red Lander +1); CHIP MAX is the 16-bit value at $87D4 + 2 x level (50, 100, 150, 200, 400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400, 4000, 6000).

entries.name: life_max
entries.what: Maximum life. The score bonus and the Energy Tank add 8, capped at $FF; the demo starts at $80.

entries.name: life
entries.what: Current life; the score bonus sets it to $47.

entries.name: life_shown
entries.what: The life meter's displayed value: steps one toward $48 per frame as the HUD redraws. The ship takes damage only while it equals $48, and dies only when a hit empties $48 with this already 0.

entries.name: attack_shield
entries.what: Attack and shield levels (1-4); $FD4B gives the player's attack from $4A.

entries.name: chips
entries.what: Chips held (16-bit, the dividend in $FD77). The score bonus refills them from $4E/$4F.

entries.name: chip_max
entries.what: The number printed after CHIP MAX.

entries.name: area
entries.what: The labyrinth area, 0-10, which the HUD prints after AREA. Leaving corridor n sets it to n folded onto 1-10.

entries.name: corridor
entries.what: The corridor, 0-22; also the screen type of a labyrinth special screen ($EE1D) and the stream-table index. 22 is the final corridor.

entries.name: map_col_row
entries.what: The player's map column and row in the labyrinth, stepped by $8071 and shown as X/Y in the HUD.

entries.name: room_openings
entries.what: The labyrinth room's exits: bit 7 north, 6 west, 5 east, 4 south (map byte 1's bits 7-4, built by bank 5 $8071). Bank 3 $9045 lets the ship leave through a side only if its bit is set and that side's door byte ($58 N, $59 W, $5A E, $5B S) has low nibble 8 (no cover left). The labyrinth savestate holds $B8: north, east, south open, west walled, and bit 3 also set (what bit 3 means is not established). The older note 'the room's $B8' means this VALUE, not the address.

entries.name: item_icon
entries.what: The item a labyrinth item room holds: $A377[sub-id], an icon number.

entries.name: shop_item_standing
entries.what: In the round creature's shops (bank 2 $8500-$8640): the item the ship last stood at, taken from the object's $0680 field ($85BA); $FF when none ($8628), tested against $0680 at $8527 so the item is not offered twice.

entries.name: spawn_script
entries.what: The spawn script id of the current room (1-47).

entries.name: door_keys
entries.what: The key each exit's door needs, N W E S (the neighbour's byte 1 AND 7).

entries.name: scene
entries.what: The scene number loaded next (tiles, metatile sets, palettes).

entries.name: room_kind
entries.what: A labyrinth room's kind: $00 plain, $20 item, $40 miniboss, $60 loop gate.

entries.name: room_sub
entries.what: A room's sub-id; the flag index for items and minibosses.

entries.name: start_cleared_5F
entries.what: Cleared to 0 by the game-start code with the other per-game state ($A5, $A0, $3C, $3E, $42-$44, $70, $2E, $49), and written nowhere else in the traced code. Nothing traced reads it: a flag whose reader is not found, or a leftover.
entries.evidence: bank 0 $8078; the whole-ROM trace has no other access

entries.name: flags_60
entries.what: Bit flags; the stage-clear routine clears bits 0-1. Meaning not established.

entries.name: spawn_ptr
entries.what: The running spawn script's pointer ($7F is its bank).

entries.name: script_wait
entries.what: The spawn script's wait counter: counts new background rows while the stage scrolls, seconds when it has stopped.

entries.name: script_second
entries.what: The spawn script's frame countdown (reloaded with 60) used while the scroll is stopped, or in the labyrinth.

entries.name: toggle
entries.what: Bit 0 flips every call of bank 6 $AD9A; the bosses use it for alternating shots. Not random.

entries.name: fire_rate
entries.what: The fire-rate level 0-5 (the Consecutive Firing item adds 1, capped at 5); $87CE[$6B] gives the delay in $39. The demo starts at 2.

entries.name: cell_class
entries.what: The cell class (0-15) under the object last tested: a weapon's hit-box centre (bank 6 $8443-$846B), the ship's position in its movement test ($82F0). The ship standing on class 2 leaves the room if the exit's key is held (bank 3 $8FBF); on class 1 it picks up the blue sphere. CORRECTION: this was recorded as 'edge_state', a lead.
entries.evidence: bank 6 $846B, $82F0; bank 3 $8FBF-$9045; sphere pick-up run on the NES model

entries.name: cell_class_x
entries.what: The class of the neighbouring cell in x in the ship's movement test.

entries.name: cell_class_y
entries.what: The class of the neighbouring cell in y in the ship's movement test. CORRECTION: also listed as 'shield_slot', a lead; the D2AA collision routine does store a hit slot in $6E, so it is shared scratch.

entries.name: align_or_mask
entries.what: Bit flags a movement test builds (bit 7 x on the tile grid, bit 6 y), and the collision mask argument of $D348.

entries.name: boss_phase
entries.what: The boss phase: 0 none; 1 set up; 2 wait for the scroll; 3 spawn; 4 fight; 6 the explosion count; back to 0.
entries.evidence: bank 3 $917F-$93EE; observed 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 6 -> 0 in the corridor 0 run

entries.name: corridor_boss_flags
entries.what: $913A[corridor]: bit 7 = turn live enemies into explosions when the boss phase starts, bit 3 copied into $60.

entries.name: boss_type
entries.what: The boss object type to spawn: $9151[corridor], or command 5's operand in corridor 21.

entries.name: boss_timer
entries.what: The boss routine's frame counter (lo, hi); 90 frames after the explosions.

entries.name: boss_slot
entries.what: The object slot a boss was spawned into.

entries.name: reward_index
entries.what: Position in the 73 [threshold][icon] pairs at bank 3 $817A that 'YOU GOT ITEM' has already given, in bytes: each award does INX INX and stores it ($813A); the list ends at $92 (CPX #$92, $80E7).

entries.name: tgl_index
entries.what: Index into $ED08, the TGL game's corridor order.

entries.name: life_at_start
entries.what: $47 as the corridor began (read back by the continue path).

entries.name: saved_pos
entries.what: The map position the progress recorder keeps ($52/$53).

entries.name: art_loader_bank
entries.what: The bank holding the graphics-load stream that $E99F reads: $E9A5 switches to it (LDA $7E / JSR $D705). Command 7 ($E85E) sets 4 ($E87C: streams in bank 4); area setup in bank 5 ($A432) and bank 6 ($801E) set 5. $7F is the same for the spawn script.

entries.name: script_bank
entries.what: The bank the running spawn script lives in (5 for rooms, 4 for corridor waves).

entries.name: oam_alloc
entries.what: The sprite allocator: $80 is the next free OAM offset, $81/$82 the limits it fills between, $83 flags (bit 0 which end it fills from, flipped each frame so overflowing sprites rotate; bit 1 full; bit 7 wrapped). $CE88 hides the unused rest.

entries.name: draw_regs
entries.what: What the metasprite drawer reads: $84 y, $85 x, $86 attributes, $87 base tile. $CC34 draws a record at these.
entries.evidence: bank 7 $CBFC-$CE23; the Fleepa and Grimgrin OAM matches

entries.name: ms_ptr
entries.what: The metasprite record being drawn.

entries.name: ms_offsets_ptr
entries.what: The metasprite drawer: pointer to the shared (x, y) offset table, copied from bytes 1-2 of the record being drawn ($88/$89). $CE06 reads (x) and $CE35 (y) through it.

entries.name: ms_offset_index
entries.what: Index into the offset table ($8A/$8B): cleared per record ($CC7E), then +2 per sprite drawn ($CE1B, $CE1D) - one x and one y byte each.

entries.name: ms_tile_index
entries.what: Index into the record's tile array: starts at 3 (just past the header, $CC73), +1 per sprite. $CDF7 reads the relative tile through it; $FF skips the sprite.

entries.name: ms_attr_index
entries.what: Index into the record's attribute array: starts at 3 + sprite count ($CC7A); advances only when the attribute byte's bit 3 is clear ($CE23-$CE27), which is the run-length coding that makes a record's length not follow from its count.

entries.name: ms_count
entries.what: Sprites left to draw in the current record: the count byte with bit 7 stripped, decremented per sprite until $CC85 falls through.

entries.name: ms_attr_byte
entries.what: The attribute byte of the sprite being drawn: ORed with the object's attributes ($86 AND $E3) into OAM byte 2, and its bit 3 decides whether $8E advances.

entries.name: stage_flags
entries.what: Stage event bits - see the table below.

entries.name: row_phase
entries.what: Which row of the current row table the next background row is: the table's rows repeat, cycling this.

entries.name: nt_select
entries.what: The PPUCTRL nametable bits ($FF bits 0-1 merged with $A7/$A9), computed by $D507.

entries.name: render_enable
entries.what: The rendering bits the NMI ORs into PPUMASK after clearing them: 0 while the screen is blanked (fades, loading), $18 when it is on.

entries.name: exit_dir
entries.what: Which way the player left a labyrinth room: 0 north, 2 west, 6 east, 8 south (4 = none).

entries.name: row_transfer
entries.what: The hand-off of one background row to the NMI: 1 = write the attribute bytes ($04E8) and the first tile row ($0130) next NMI, 2 = write the second tile row ($0150), 3 = attributes and one row (the blank/marker row), 0 = nothing. $DD54 steps it.

entries.name: scroll_regs
entries.what: The scroll the game wants: $A6 vertical, $A7 its nametable bit, $A8 horizontal, $A9 its nametable bit. $D507 copies $A6 to $FC and $A8 to $FD; the corridor scroll subtracts the speed from $A6.

entries.name: row_attr_lo
entries.what: The low byte of the attribute address of the background row being built ($C0 | (($AE x 2) AND $1C) x 2); ground objects keep it ($0608).

entries.name: row_nt_half
entries.what: Flips each time the row counter $AE wraps; while 1 the row address is moved up by $0800, so the corridor's rows alternate between $2000 and its mirror $2800 (vertical mirroring makes them the same table).
entries.evidence: bank 7 $E6B9-$E6C5, $E98F-area; 216 writes to $2800-$2BFF in 120 corridor frames

entries.name: row_ppu_addr
entries.what: The PPU address of the first tile row of the background row being built ($2000 + $40 x $AE, +$0800 while $AB is 1, or OR $17 in the labyrinth): $AC low, $AD high. A ground object takes a copy so it can patch its own tiles.

entries.name: row_index
entries.what: Which of the 15 background rows (16 lines each) is being built, 14 down to 0 and round again; in the labyrinth, which pair of tile rows of the room is being drawn.

entries.name: row_pixels
entries.what: Pixels scrolled within the current 16-pixel background row.

entries.name: row_counter
entries.what: The stage clock: background rows since the corridor began. Stream records fire when it equals their trigger.

entries.name: stream_next_trigger
entries.what: Bank 4's screen-data engine: the trigger (a stage row) of the record about to run. Loaded from the block's first two bytes ($E593), compared with the row counter $B0/$B1 at $E6D0/$E6D6 (a match fires the record), and reloaded from the two bytes after each record's operands ($E89D).

entries.name: stream_row_table
entries.what: Pointer to the row table that command 1 selects ($E721 reads it from the record; $A1 is reset to 0). $E8AB indexes it with the row cycle $A1 to build each new row's 16 metatile ids.

entries.name: scroll_acc
entries.what: The scroll position accumulator (fraction, whole) the speed is subtracted from.

entries.name: scroll_step
entries.what: The whole pixels the scroll moved this frame, from the speed in $B8/$B9.

entries.name: scroll_speed
entries.what: The scroll speed in 1/256 pixel a frame, ramped 2/256 a frame toward $BA/$BB.

entries.name: scroll_target
entries.what: The speed command 0 sets the scroll toward (bit 7 of the high byte: at once).

entries.name: stream_ptr
entries.what: The pointer into the corridor's event stream (bank 4).

entries.name: split_addr_tmp
entries.what: Scratch for the corridor's split marker: sprite 0's Y ($0200) + the vertical scroll $FC + 1, wrapped at $F0 and rounded to a tile row ($DCA8-$DCBA), then shifted into a PPU address ($2000 + 32 x row) that is loaded into $2006 so $DCCE can write the solid tile $FE there.

entries.name: room_north_west
entries.what: The map records of the north ($E0) and west ($E2) neighbours of the current room.

entries.name: room_ptr
entries.what: The current room's map record.

entries.name: room_east_south
entries.what: The east ($E6) and south ($E8) neighbours' records.

entries.name: demo_timer
entries.what: The demo's timer; it also counts the credits screens.

entries.name: demo_pattern_timer
entries.what: The demo's input generator ($DAE1): frames until the next pattern change, reloaded with 24-39 (random AND $0F + $18). Bank 0 reuses $F0-$F4 as timers/counters in the title code ($8160-$8424), which is not worked out.

entries.name: demo_pattern
entries.what: The demo's current input pattern (a byte of $DB32-$DB51), copied into the pad bytes $F7/$F8 each frame while $30 bit 7 is set. Bank 0's title code also counts with it ($8415).

entries.name: demo_pattern_index
entries.what: The demo's index into the 32 patterns: random at start ($8170), then (AND $1F) + 1 at each change.

entries.name: pads_new
entries.what: Buttons newly pressed, pads 1 and 2 (A = $80 ... Right = $01).

entries.name: pads_held
entries.what: Buttons held. A and B held at reset ($F7 = $C0) starts the sound test.

entries.name: scroll_shadow
entries.what: What the NMI writes to $2005: $FD horizontal (written first), $FC vertical. The raster-split IRQ adds $FC to sprite 0's Y.

entries.name: ppumask_shadow
entries.what: The PPUMASK value the game wants.

entries.name: ppuctrl_shadow
entries.what: The PPUCTRL value the game wants; bit 7 is the NMI enable the wait loops test.

entries.name: ppu_queue
entries.what: The PPU write queue, staged here: [count][ppu_hi][ppu_lo][data...]. The count byte's top two bits give the type - under $80 a run with increment 1, $80-$BF increment 32, $C0 and up an attribute read-modify-write. (The stack shares this page and grows down from $01FF.)

entries.name: password_work
entries.what: The password decoder's 24 output bytes, borrowing the PPU queue's staging area.

entries.name: map_row_buffer
entries.what: The status screen's map row buffer: a quadrant mask per tile, flushed every second row.

entries.name: score
entries.what: The score, six decimal digits, one a byte, in tens: a fixed 0 is printed after them. $0170 is the 1,000,000s digit.

entries.name: status_saved
entries.what: The weapon selected, and sprite 0's Y, saved while the status screen is up.

entries.name: bonus_threshold
entries.what: The next score-bonus threshold, three digits, compared with $0170-$0172. $017C = $FF ends the bonuses.
entries.evidence: bank 7 $DF3D; bank 0 $80A5-$80B3; run at chosen scores

entries.name: palette_dirty
entries.what: Set to 3 after code edits the palette shadow ($0180-$0198); the flush is not followed.

entries.name: palette_shadow
entries.what: The palette the game wants: the backdrop, then 8 palettes of 3 colours (4 background, 4 sprite).
entries.evidence: bank 5 $B2E4; two savestates; the cutscene's backdrop flash writes $0180

entries.name: palette_slots
entries.what: Eight palette slot indices the stream's command 8 writes.

entries.name: oam
entries.what: The OAM shadow, copied by DMA every NMI. Sprite 0 is the HUD's raster-split marker; $02F0-$02FF are the status screen's and the credits' own.
entries.evidence: bank 7 NMI; the OAM matches in three savestates

entries.name: sound_event
entries.what: The song-event register. A song's $94 command ORs its operand into it (the title song sets $10 after one pass), and when a channel's stream ends the channel's song number ($03DD) is stored here. The boss routine and the title loop wait for it to become non-zero.

entries.name: sound_cmd
entries.what: Sound control bits: bit 0 requests a restart (clears it, reloads song 0 and marks every channel); bit 1 makes channel 6 run instead of 5.

entries.name: sound_channel
entries.what: The channel the tick is working on (5 down to 0, or 6).

entries.name: sound_ysave
entries.what: The stream index saved by handlers that borrow Y.

entries.name: sound_song
entries.what: The song number being started ($97E4); a loop counter while a header is copied.

entries.name: sound_tmp
entries.what: Scratch: the header's first byte, and the envelope's output volume.

entries.name: sound_busy
entries.what: The mask of the four hardware channels in use.

entries.name: sound_paused
entries.what: While non-zero the tick returns at once; $97CC raises it around a song start.

entries.name: apu_shadow
entries.what: The APU register shadow, flushed to $4000-$400F; $FF means skip.

entries.name: sound_ctl
entries.what: ORed with each active channel's control byte during a tick, bit 5 = a channel muted all.

entries.name: sound_channels
entries.what: Seven soft channels, 33 fields each: field f of channel c is at $0319 + 7 f + c. The field table below names them.

entries.name: cell_map_or_overlay_slots
entries.what: Two uses of one block. In the labyrinth: the room's 16 x 12 cell classes, one nibble a cell (even column in the high nibble), built when the room is drawn (bank 5 $8354) and changed as weapons break blocks (bank 6 $8523). In a corridor: the eight overlay slots (structures placed over the background): column, repeat count, height, row pointer.

entries.name: password_field
entries.what: The password screen's 32 characters, each a grid index. Shares the page with the overlay slots, which are not in use on that screen.

entries.name: password_payload
entries.what: The decoded password payload; index i is read to $0439 + i.

entries.name: set_ptr_lo
entries.what: The low bytes of the eight loaded metatile set windows.

entries.name: set_ptr_hi
entries.what: The high bytes of the same pointers.

entries.name: set_tile_base
entries.what: Each set's tile base.

entries.name: set_spawn_list
entries.what: Each set's spawn list: 0-2, an index into the three pointers at bank 5 $803C. The corridor spawner uses it.

entries.name: loaded_block
entries.what: The tile block loaded in each art slot.

entries.name: loaded_tile
entries.what: The tile position each art slot loaded to.

entries.name: item_flags
entries.what: One flag per item room and miniboss, set when taken or beaten; the password carries them.

entries.name: areas_cleared
entries.what: One bit per corridor, set when its boss is beaten; hides the entrance marker.

entries.name: weapon_levels
entries.what: Two bits a weapon, weapon 1 in the low bits of $04AC.

entries.name: eraser_count
entries.what: Weapon 12 (the Enemy Eraser)'s stock.

entries.name: keys
entries.what: The keys held, bit k-1 for key k.

entries.name: corridor_seals
entries.what: The corridor seals: bit c-1 set = the seal on corridor c is removed (corridors 1-8 in $04B1, 9 and 10 in $04B2). Set through the helper $C078/$EFC7 (A = n gives Y = n >> 3 and A = 1 << (n AND 7)) by $A245, which ten routines in bank 5 ($A1C4 table, index = corridor - 1) reach when their condition is met: 50 shot hits on the gate (1, 5), the ship touching four zones (2), 20 s in the room (3), the round creature's rooms entered with an alternating move history (4, $9FD8), the chip count changing (6), the same history in the gate room (7), weapon NO USE + A (8), the ship on the gate (9), B held 10 s (10). A set bit makes the gate's second half open the first and remove itself ($A1AA) and the ship can enter the corridor. Corridors 11-20 have no seal. Cleared bits for the bosses are the separate array $04A9. Cleared by the game-start code at bank 0 $80A5/$80A8 and NOT part of the password payload ($04A0-$04B0): after a password they would start clear, unless that start code is skipped (not checked). CORRECTION: first recorded as 'once_flags', ten one-shot events.
entries.evidence: bank 5 $A19B-$A25B, $A245-$A24D, $9FD8, $A041, $A0A1; bank 7 $EFC7; run on the model through the real $EE1D room setup, all ten conditions driven (see the Labyrinth page, #seals)

entries.name: tgl_total
entries.what: The TGL game's running score total, six digits; / 10,000 gives the reward index $15.

entries.name: corridor_score
entries.what: The score as a corridor began; the boss turns it into the points gained, ticking 10 off every 64 frames.

entries.name: row_cells
entries.what: The 16 cells of the background row being built: metatile ids, then (after drawing) each metatile's fifth byte, which the ground-object spawner reads.
entries.evidence: bank 7 $E8AB; bank 5 $83B3, $89FB; the corridor 0 spawn trace

entries.name: palette_saved
entries.what: The palette, saved while a screen fades or the status screen is up.

entries.name: row_attr_bytes
entries.what: The eight attribute-table bytes of the background row being built (corridor). Bank 5 $8442-$8454 merges each metatile's palette bits into them (read-modify-write with the mask tables $8469/$846D and the replicated-palette patterns at $0199); the NMI writes all eight to the PPU in one run at the address from $AA ($DD83-$DDAD).

entries.name: move_history
entries.what: The last ten moves in the labyrinth, one direction pushed per move; the loop gates sum them.

base_artifacts.reason: Base of indexed accesses with Y of 1 or more: the score digits $0170-$0175 are cleared with STA $016F,Y (bank 0 $809C, $80EC) and the top three compared with LDA $016F,Y at bank 7 $DF45.
Base of SBC $017B,Y at bank 7 $DF48: reads the bonus threshold $017C-$017E beside the score digits.

PPU queue bytes: the unrolled eight-byte copy at bank 7 $DDC0-$DE01 reads LDA $0130,Y ... $0137,Y and writes each to $2007, so these are the 7th and 8th data bytes of a queue entry at offset Y, not variables.

object_fields.name: type
object_fields.what: The object type; bit 7 is set once its handler has initialised it.

object_fields.name: y
object_fields.what: Y position.
object_fields.evidence: bank 7 $CBFC; the Grimgrin and Fleepa OAM matches

object_fields.name: x
object_fields.what: X position.

object_fields.name: metasprite
object_fields.what: The metasprite id to draw.

object_fields.name: attributes
object_fields.what: Sprite attributes: palette in bits 0-1, bit 6 flips horizontally, bit 7 vertically.

object_fields.name: collision_flags
object_fields.what: Which sides it collides with (from $D02C); bit 7 skips it. The boss runs zero the player's to make it untouchable.

object_fields.name: hp
object_fields.what: Hit points (from $D0AB).

object_fields.name: attack
object_fields.what: Damage it deals on contact (from $D12A).

object_fields.name: yvel_frac
object_fields.what: Y velocity, fractional byte.

object_fields.name: yvel
object_fields.what: Y velocity, signed whole byte.

object_fields.name: xvel_frac
object_fields.what: X velocity, fractional byte.

object_fields.name: xvel
object_fields.what: X velocity, signed whole byte.

object_fields.name: draw_flags
object_fields.what: Drawing flags (from $D1A9), tested bit by bit by the drawer.

object_fields.name: phase
object_fields.what: Animation / phase counter, whole part ($CD7A: add A, wrap at Y).

object_fields.name: phase_frac
object_fields.what: The phase counter's fraction.

object_fields.name: target_y
object_fields.what: The y the object accelerates toward ($CD12), or a direction number the aim routine returned - handlers reuse it.

object_fields.name: target_x
object_fields.what: The x the object accelerates toward ($CD46).

object_fields.name: param
object_fields.what: A spawn parameter handlers pass to the thing they create (a shot's speed class). Meaning varies.

object_fields.name: param2
object_fields.what: A second parameter, set from a per-variant table by the shot handler. Meaning not established.

object_fields.name: base_tile
object_fields.what: The base tile the drawer adds to a metasprite's relative tiles ($87).

object_fields.name: box_x_min
object_fields.what: Hitbox: x minus the metasprite's half width.

object_fields.name: box_x_max
object_fields.what: Hitbox: x plus the half width.

object_fields.name: box_y_min
object_fields.what: Hitbox: y minus the half height.

object_fields.name: box_y_max
object_fields.what: Hitbox: y plus the half height.

object_fields.name: aux_hp
object_fields.what: The high part of the hit points ($D385 shifts the hit points into it) and the type an object had when it died.

object_fields.name: pos_frac
object_fields.what: A position fraction added to the y velocity's fraction by some handlers.

object_fields.name: unknown_26
object_fields.what: Not named.

object_fields.name: timer
object_fields.what: A countdown handlers use first: an entry timer, a shot direction, a spawned shot's aim.

object_fields.name: state
object_fields.what: A state or counter: the boss's state byte, a spawned shot's variant.

object_fields.name: aux3
object_fields.what: Per-handler scratch (a fire delay, a stage index).

object_fields.name: aux4
object_fields.what: Per-handler scratch (an animation length, a mask).

object_fields.name: block_base
object_fields.what: The tile block base the object's art loaded to; $CF8D copies it from $06C8 at spawn, handlers move $06C8 and leave this.

$30.what: Demo (attract mode): set by the demo's setup and tested at $EB9C and by the award code.
A corridor or a special screen is running (set at corridor start by $EF97 = ORA #$50, and by $F2C3 = ORA #$48).
A labyrinth special screen: the room drawer takes its special path.
Tested in the NMI; set at corridor start with bit 6.
Set with bit 6 when a corridor loads; cleared at $F446.
Quiet: no score-bonus jingle ($DF80); set while the score is zeroed at game start.

$A0.what: End of stage: set when a boss is beaten (corridor) or a room exit is taken; the scroll step tests it and jumps to $EB18.
The player died (or left a labyrinth room): tested at $EB8C.
A new background row came in: set by the row builder, cleared by $E659; spawn waits count it.
A draw or flush request: $DD54 calls $D507 when it is set.

sound_fields.name: control
sound_fields.what: Channel control: 0 = idle. Bits 0-1 take the duty from the note sequence; bit 4 is tested when a note starts.

sound_fields.name: volume
sound_fields.what: The register's volume (low nibble, clamped 0-15) and flag bits (high nibble); bit 4 enables the volume envelope.

sound_fields.name: vol_envelope
sound_fields.what: Volume envelope id (0 = none); its table is $99AB.

sound_fields.name: pitch_envelope
sound_fields.what: Pitch envelope id (bit 7 none, bit 6 changes how the result is applied); its table is $995F.

sound_fields.name: transpose
sound_fields.what: A pitch offset added to the note number; commands add to it.

sound_fields.name: tick_reload
sound_fields.what: The tick countdown's reload value.

sound_fields.name: hw_channel
sound_fields.what: The hardware channel wanted (compared with 3 for the triangle).

sound_fields.name: stream_lo
sound_fields.what: The stream pointer, low byte (high in field 8).

sound_fields.name: stream_hi
sound_fields.what: The stream pointer, high byte.

sound_fields.name: flags
sound_fields.what: Bit 0 software-rate mode; bit 1 volume fade reached its target; bit 3 a note sequence is running; bit 5 volume fade on; bit 6 slide direction down; bit 7 pitch slide on.

sound_fields.name: position
sound_fields.what: Ticks counted in the current note.

sound_fields.name: length
sound_fields.what: The current note's length in ticks; reaching it ends the note.

sound_fields.name: last_duration
sound_fields.what: The last duration byte read, kept for a repeat.

sound_fields.name: countdown
sound_fields.what: The tick countdown for the note.

sound_fields.name: last_length
sound_fields.what: The previous note's length, reused when a note has no duration byte.

sound_fields.name: out_volume
sound_fields.what: The volume to send to the APU after the envelope is applied.

sound_fields.name: note
sound_fields.what: Used with the note number when a pitch is looked up; not followed further.

sound_fields.name: unknown_17
sound_fields.what: Not named.

sound_fields.name: soft_rate
sound_fields.what: The software tick accumulator's step (command sets it and the accumulator to $80).

sound_fields.name: soft_acc
sound_fields.what: The software tick accumulator; a carry advances the note.

sound_fields.name: vol_env_pos
sound_fields.what: Position in the volume envelope.

sound_fields.name: pitch_env_pos
sound_fields.what: Position in the pitch envelope; zeroed at each note.

sound_fields.name: period_lo
sound_fields.what: The timer period sent to the APU, low byte.

sound_fields.name: period_hi
sound_fields.what: The timer period, high byte (a slide stops at 8).

sound_fields.name: fade_rate
sound_fields.what: Volume fade step added each tick.

sound_fields.name: fade_acc
sound_fields.what: The volume fade's accumulator; a carry steps the volume.

sound_fields.name: fade_target
sound_fields.what: The volume the fade moves toward.

sound_fields.name: slide_shift
sound_fields.what: A pitch slide's step: the period shifted right by this many bits.

sound_fields.name: song_id
sound_fields.what: The song number playing on the channel; stored in $0300 when its stream ends.

sound_fields.name: state
sound_fields.what: Bit 7 set at each note start and cleared each tick; bit 6 set to mute the channel.

sound_fields.name: seq_value
sound_fields.what: The current byte of a note sequence: its bits 5-6 give the duty.

sound_fields.name: seq_lo
sound_fields.what: The note sequence pointer, low byte (command $90; a 00 byte jumps).

sound_fields.name: seq_hi
sound_fields.what: The note sequence pointer, high byte.
